# Every value below is read from the LIVE source, not from a
# record. The IMPLICIT ZERO enumerators are the ones a careless
# reading would miss, so they are called out explicitly.

YES (the first enumerator after the explicit -1; it is the ZERO of the enum)

column1: # IR_TYPE_VOID is the ZERO of IrValueType and IR_CMP_EQ is the
# ZERO of IrCmpKind. A zero discriminant is therefore a LEGITIMATE
# input value, and a status/data separation that used zero as a
# failure marker would collide with it. This is the concrete
# reason clause E15 requires an explicit status/data separation
# for any candidate whose ABI carries a discriminant.

column2: I64 IrCmpKind x I64 is_float (a bounded, copied scalar pair)
column3: NO pointer crosses the seam; the seam carries scalars only

column2: a bounded copied code string, or an explicit NULL for an out-of-domain kind
column3: the output is an immutable literal owned by the PolyC side; the host never frees it and never writes through it

column2: the x86_64 tables return NULL for an unsupported kind and the CALLER turns that into an explicit panic; the AArch64 tables PANIC in the default arm
column3: a negative status is NOT used, so a legitimate zero discriminant (IR_CMP_EQ) can never be confused with a failure

column2: TOTAL: the domain is closed over the enum; an out-of-domain kind fails loudly, never silently
a copied scalar IrValueType (or a copied scalar AST-type descriptor for irConvertType)
column3: NO pointer crosses the seam; the AST type is projected to scalars BEFORE the call
